title: Guardrails before bulk operations.
body: Destructive commands ship with a required confirm flag, batch caps, mandatory filters, and value thresholds. I design for the day someone runs the wrong command against tens of thousands of racks.

proof.label: racks in the first guarded sweep

title: Compute on read when decisions can't wait for exports.
body: I replaced lagging batch analytics with computation over live data, filtered at the source, so operations and finance decide from the same current numbers.

title: Agents orchestrate tools; they don't replace them.
body: My LLM agent reuses the platform's existing commands instead of inventing new write paths, and AI-assisted audits end in human verification against real data.

title: The simplest viable design goes first.
body: A carrier-grade router system went through several elaborate proposals before the simple one shipped. Now the boring design is the baseline every alternative has to beat on a named risk.

proof.label: saved per year by the design that shipped

title: Assert on outputs, not just inputs.
body: Classification logic now ships with checks on what it produces (totals, match counts, unmatched rows), so the next defect fails a check the day it lands.

proof.label: a defect survived without output checks
